parsed.summary: The Lean theorem states that every complex polynomial f with 0 < degree f has a complex root, i.e. some z with f.eval z = 0. This is exactly the fundamental theorem of algebra. Here degree is WithBot ℕ, and the zero polynomial has degree ⊥, so it is excluded, as are nonzero constants. No meaningful caveat.

glossary.plain: degree of f in WithBot ℕ; deg 0 = ⊥, and 0 < degree f means f is non-constant

lean_claims.plain: For every f ∈ ℂ[X] with deg f > 0, there exists z ∈ ℂ with f(z) = 0.

paper_claims.plain: Every non-constant complex polynomial has a complex root.

coverage.why: For a complex polynomial, 0 < degree f holds exactly when f is non-constant.
